html:
Azerbaijan is a country in the South Caucasus on the west shore of the Caspian Sea, with its capital at Baku. The map shows it in 1914, from 1920 to 1930, and again from 1994.

The land had long been ruled by Persian states. Russia took it from Qajar Iran in two wars, fixed by the Treaty of Turkmenchay in 1828, which drew the border on the Aras River. Azerbaijanis therefore live on both sides: in the north under Russia, and in north-western Iran. Around 1900 Baku became one of the world's great oil centres.

When the Russian Empire fell, the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic was declared in 1918, one of the first secular democracies in the Muslim world. The Red Army conquered it in 1920, and it became a Soviet republic within the USSR.

It regained independence as the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991. It lost a war with Armenia over Nagorno-Karabakh, then took the region back by force in 2020 and 2023. Heydar Aliyev and his son Ilham have ruled since 1993, funded by oil and gas.
sum: Azerbaijan is a country in the South Caucasus on the west shore of the Caspian Sea, with its capital at Baku. The map shows it in 1914, from 1920 to 1930, and again from 1994.
